parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: By reference to the direction of propagation of energy, state what is meant by a $transverse$ wave.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
Circular water waves may be produced by vibrating dippers at points $P$ and $Q$, as illustrated in Fig. 4.1.
{{figure:figure_4_1}}
Fig. 4.1 (not to scale)
The waves from $P$ alone have the same amplitude at point $R$ as the waves from $Q$ alone. Distance $PR$ is $44\text{ cm}$ and distance $QR$ is $29\text{ cm}$.
The dippers vibrate in phase with a period of $1.5\text{ s}$ to produce waves of speed $4.0\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Determine the wavelength of the waves.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: By reference to the distances $PR$ and $QR$, explain why the water particles are at rest at point $R$.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text:
The wave has intensity $I_1$ at distance $x = 2.0\text{ cm}$ and intensity $I_2$ at $x = 10.0\text{ cm}$.
Determine the ratio
$$\frac{\text{intensity } I_2}{\text{intensity } I_1}.$$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the phase difference, with its unit, between the oscillations of the liquid particles at distances $x = 3.0\text{ cm}$ and $x = 4.0\text{ cm}$.
